findings.title: Require a receipt to match a supplied candidate digest
findings.expected: When the current candidate and request include candidate_digest, an assurance or closure receipt must carry that same digest. A receipt lacking that binding must not satisfy the gate.
findings.actual: sameCandidate skips candidate_digest whenever either operand lacks it. A schema-valid receipt without candidate_digest returns PASS / independent_assurance_verified with gate_eligible true, even though the current candidate and request carry a digest. A wrong digest is rejected, but deleting it changes the verdict to PASS.
findings.reachability: The new exported evaluateVerification evaluator calls sameCandidate for receipt versus request and current candidate at lines 213-214 before its assurance PASS. The reference policy designates this module as its runtime evaluator; no native host wiring is claimed. This matters for changed binaries or uncommitted work at an unchanged revision, including the review's own candidate identity pattern: the digest distinguishes the actual tree from other work at the same HEAD.

reproduction.method: Direct in-process invocation on the pinned product, with no file mutations.
reproduction.setup: Use the valid independent assurance request/receipt shape from test/verification.test.mjs: matching candidate_ref, candidate_revision, claim_id, backend, command_configuration, status VERIFIED, authority assurance, independent produced_by identity/session, available enabled backend, and gate assurance. Supply the same 64-hex candidate_digest on candidate, request, and receipt.
steps: Evaluate the matching input: PASS and gate_eligible true.
Change only receipt.candidate_digest to another valid 64-hex digest: REJECT / candidate_mismatch.
Delete only receipt.candidate_digest: PASS / independent_assurance_verified and gate_eligible true.
reproduction.schema_check: Installed jsonschema Draft202012Validator reports zero errors for both the request and the receipt with the digest omitted.

findings.title: Resolve assurance units for the configured slice and lifecycle cadences
findings.expected: The approved slice, phase, and lifecycle cadences must each admit the corresponding declared unit once and retain its spent budget. An existing slice or Lifecycle must not need an owner amendment merely to use an already-approved cadence.
findings.actual: The new cadence branch permits a slice request past the initial guard, but declaredUnits still returns only waves[].id, phases[].phaseId, or direct. A declared S1 slice and a declared L1 Lifecycle are rejected as undeclared_review_unit. The same fixture's phase P1 passes. The documented runtime policy likewise still excludes slice identity from the budget key.
findings.introduced_basis: Slice/lifecycle configurability is introduced by this candidate's changed cadence guard, policy, schema, and public contract; the prior wave-only unit resolver was not adapted to that new behavior.
findings.reachability: hooks/transition-order.cjs evaluate({action_kind:'assurance_transition', assurance}) calls evaluateAssuranceBudget. The same evaluator is used for EVIDENCE_READY -> REVIEWING. Thus an Orchestrator performing the documented procedural check receives BLOCK on valid newly supported cadence choices.

reproduction.method: Temporary declaration and task-record JSON under a disposable system temp directory; invoke the real transition evaluator.
reproduction.request: assurance = {journey:'L1', unit_kind:'slice', request_scope:'slice', cadence:'slice', assurance_unit:'S1', declaration_path, task_record_path}
reproduction.explanation: For the phase control, use unit_kind/request_scope/cadence phase and assurance_unit P1. For the lifecycle case, use lifecycle and L1. The unit resolver never reads lifecycle_id or slices, regardless of their declared cadence.

findings.title: Prevent embedded SVG styles from changing the surrounding Manifest
findings.expected: A sanitized prepared model view must not alter or hide the Manifest's risk, authority, evidence, or navigation content outside that view.
findings.actual: sanitizeSvg preserves unrestricted stylesheet selectors and declarations, then renderModelFigure inserts that SVG directly into the HTML document. A valid digest-bound model containing '#s8, #s9 { display: none !important; }' renders successfully and retains a rule targeting the Manifest's risk and authority sections.
findings.reachability: Both file-backed and inline selected/required SVG views pass through loadView -> sanitizeSvg -> renderModelFigure -> renderDodManifest. The generated document contains section IDs s8 and s9. SVG 2 section 6.4 specifies that SVG style sheets in an HTML document apply to all HTML and inline SVG content, so placement inside the figure does not scope the stylesheet.

reproduction.method: In-process renderDodManifest with a synthetic selected/required model; no browser, network request, or product write.
reproduction.setup: Supply a dod_manifest with title Fixture, template_version 1.0.0, output_name fixture-dod-manifest.html, and models [{id:'M1',required:true,selected:true,render_status:'READY',digest:sha256Hex(svg),view:{format:'svg',inline:svg}}]. Include an OPEN risk row.
reproduction.selector_check: Installed cssselect2 matches the preserved selectors to HTML sections s8 and s9. The visibility consequence follows SVG 2 section 6.4 and the retained display:none!important declaration; this is standards-based static proof, not a claimed browser observation.

findings.bounded_repair_target: Constrain or isolate SVG stylesheet effects in tools/render-dod-manifest.mjs so they cannot select the containing Manifest or other model views. Add a focused renderer regression for cross-document selectors while preserving safe prepared-view appearance.

findings.title: Reject CSS-escaped external imports in sanitized SVG
findings.expected: External resource references must remain rejected after CSS parsing, including escaped forms, so a rendered Manifest is self-contained and cannot load a remote stylesheet from an embedded model.
findings.actual: The stylesheet filter searches raw CSS for literal @import and url(. It does not decode CSS escapes. '@im\70ort "https://example.invalid/model.css";' survives sanitizeSvg and full renderDodManifest with a matching digest; a CSS parser recognizes it as an import rule.
findings.reachability: A prepared inline or file-backed SVG is accepted through the normal digest-checked renderer path. Its emitted style element is active CSS in the containing HTML. CSS Syntax defines hexadecimal escapes in identifiers; CSS Cascade defines import rules as stylesheet inclusion. No attacker-supplied digest mismatch is needed because the renderer is expected to sanitize the bytes it binds.

reproduction.method: In-process SVG sanitization and complete Manifest rendering, followed by an installed CSS parser; no URL was contacted.
reproduction.setup: Use the same minimal selected/required model fixture as S7-003, with the SHA-256 of these exact SVG bytes.
reproduction.parser: tinycss2 1.5.1 parse_stylesheet(css, skip_whitespace=True, skip_comments=True)[0] returns type at-rule, lower_at_keyword import, and string URL https://example.invalid/model.css.
reproduction.scope_note: Distinct from S7-003: restricting selector scope alone does not prevent loading a remote stylesheet.

findings.bounded_repair_target: Make the CSS safety checks in tools/render-dod-manifest.mjs fail closed for escaped/import/resource-bearing CSS across stylesheet and style-attribute entry points. Add a focused escaped-import regression; retain the approved standard-library implementation constraint.

findings.title: Quote the Copilot hook script path after plugin-root expansion
findings.expected: The newly shipped SessionStart and Stop hooks must run when the plugin's absolute installation path contains spaces.
findings.actual: Both commands concatenate an unquoted ${PLUGIN_ROOT} into a shell command. With a plugin root named 'plugin with spaces', Node receives only the path prefix as its script and exits 1 with MODULE_NOT_FOUND; neither hook emits its advisory JSON.
findings.reachability: VS Code discovers this exact com.github.copilot hook file for the root Agent Plugins manifest, expands PLUGIN_ROOT to the absolute plugin path, and executes hook commands through a shell. Spaces in a user or installation directory therefore affect the shipped command directly. This is a package command defect, not an upstream host defect.

reproduction.method: Read the shipped hook commands, create a disposable symlink to the unchanged plugin under a temporary 'plugin with spaces' directory, expand PLUGIN_ROOT, and run each command through the shell with its event JSON and an empty temporary cwd.
reproduction.control: Invoke node with the complete same script path as a single argv element: both events exit 0 and emit valid JSON.
reproduction.cleanup: Temporary symlink and fixture directory removed.
reproduction.limitation: Reproduced the documented shell invocation rather than launching a native VS Code session.

findings.bounded_repair_target: Quote the complete script argument in both com.github.copilot/hooks/hooks.json commands and add a focused path-with-spaces execution case in test/host-mapping.test.mjs. Preserve the existing partial activation/closeout-only mapping.
